newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil states press gov't for debt deals-report.
newsitem.headline: Brazil states press gov't for debt deals-report.

text.p: Governors of more than a dozen Brazilian states met in Sao Paulo Monday to forge a united front in their bid to persuade the government to refinance their massive debts, private Invest News agency reported.
The governors said they were seeking debt refinancing in line with recent deals struck with Minas Gerais and Rio Grande do Sul.

"The stabilization plan won't be fully successful unless we solve the problem of the debts of the states, which is inhibiting our capacity to invest," Invest News quoted Rio de Janeiro governor Marcello Alencar as saying.

Last month, Brasilia agreed to restructure 8.6 billion reais of Minas Gerais' debt and 6.0 billion reais for Rio Grande do Sul. Both involved 30-year refinancing terms and interest per year of 6.0 percent, adjusted for inflation.
In return, the states must carry out fiscal adjustments and retire 20 percent of their debt stock through asset sales.

At least 12 of Brazil's states are thought to be virtually bankrupt, unable to pay interest on federal loans. The total net debt of the states and municipalities stood at 83.99 billion reais in July, up from 81.926 billion reais in June.
The governor of Amazonas sate, Amazonino Mendes, said in Sao Paulo that the meeting was not meant to pressure the government but to strike a common position.
"There's no hostility towards the government," he told Invest News.
Invest News said 20 governors of Brazilian states were expected to attend the meeting.
